newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Shekel representative rate breaks 3.3 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Shekel representative rate breaks 3.3 per dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed lower against the dollar on Thursday as the U.S. currency rose above 3.3 shekels for the first time since June, dealers said.

"The dollar continues to rise abroad but on a slower pace. This is putting lots of pressure on the basket which fell again to more than seven percent below the diagonal rate," said a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.
"The central bank had to buy dollars to support the basket on a relatively high scale," the deal said.
Dealers estimated that Bank of Israel bought more than $100 million in foreign currency on Thursday in addition to $500 million the bank spent last week supporting the basket.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3030 shekels against 3.2970 shekels on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6224 shekels against 3.6218 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7693 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7747 on Tuesday and against the mark at 2.0120 shekels against 2.0094 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3040 shekels.
